briefing:
Alright, drag me out of bed for this, I guess. More "breakthroughs" you say? Fantastic. Seems we're on the cusp of a quantum computing revolution fueled by… tiny flaws in diamonds. Because obviously, the hardest material on Earth is just what we need to make an already-esoteric field even more absurd. Meanwhile, someone's finally figured out magnetism could *dramatically* reduce the energy needed for AI chips. Shocking. Turns out we might need to conserve power after building server farms the size of small nations to train LLMs on every scraped selfie on the internet. And just in case we weren't feeling insignificant enough, scientists are now simulating how the universe emerged from darkness. Great. While they're recreating 2 billion years of cosmic history, I'm still trying to get *this* monolith to compile without pulling in six conflicting versions of Log4j. Priorities, people.

Speaking of things that actually exist: your unhackable, decentralized crypto dreams? Yeah, someone just confirmed that "secure" Trezor hardware wallets had actual, physical implants designed to steal your precious recovery phrase over cellular. Because of course they did. Turns out the real world with soldering irons and supply chains is still a thing, no matter how many chains you shove on a ledger. And not to be outdone, German military drone operations got "disrupted" by a cyberattack. "Hostile actors," they say. Probably just a script kiddie who got bored and found the admin password taped to a monitor. "Swiftly resolved," I bet.

Then there's the truly groundbreaking news: Check Point security gateways, those bastions of corporate network defense, got pwned via a PHP2Shell vulnerability to deploy data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts. PHP2Shell, for crying out loud! What year is it? This isn't just "hostile actors," this is a full-blown existential crisis for enterprise security. But hey, at least they found "political messages" during the destruction, so it's not just pure incompetence, it's *motivated* incompetence. Just another Tuesday in the trenches, I suppose. Pour me another, I need to go debug why our "groundbreaking AI" can't tell a cat from a toaster.

evidence.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
evidence.facts:
• A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors.
• Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
• The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications.

evidence.title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
evidence.facts:
• A promising new approach to building computer chips could dramatically reduce the energy needed for computing, including the rapidly growing demands of artificial intelligence.
• At the center of the breakthrough is a special class of materials known as multiferroics, which combine electrical and magnetic properties that can be controlled together using extremely small voltages.
• These materials could make future electronics far more energy efficient than today's technology.

evidence.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
evidence.facts:
• A powerful new computer simulation is allowing scientists to explore one of the most mysterious periods in cosmic history, when the universe emerged from darkness and the first stars and galaxies began to transform the cosmos.
• Developed by researchers at MIT, Harvard University, and other institutions, the simulation, called Lumina, recreates the evolution of the early universe across a region roughly 1.6 billion light-years wide.
• It follows 2 billion years of cosmic history, revealing how galaxies formed, how radiation spread through space, and how the universe gradually became transparent to light.

evidence.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
evidence.facts:
• Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Trezor has confirmed that three Safe 5 devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to steal wallet recovery phrases and send them to attackers over cellular networks.
• The findings follow an investigation into a suspected hardware implant first reported in October, when a customer discovered an unauthorized circuit board inside a Trezor Safe 5 purchased from Indonesian reseller CryptoBilis.
• At the time, Trezor had not received the device for examination and could not confirm the implant's capabilities.

evidence.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
evidence.facts:
• German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed that it detected an incident in late October that was part of an active cyberattack by "hostile actors."
• The company responded quickly, working with relevant authorities to resolve the issue swiftly and ensure its unmanned systems could safely resume operations.
• Quantum Systems is a German defense technology company that builds reconnaissance and interceptor drones, along with other unmanned systems and the software that controls them.

evidence.title: Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper
evidence.facts:
• Vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway instances have been targeted in PHP2Shell attacks that deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts.
• The attacks started on October 30, initially against Israeli organizations, and were conducted by an actor that ran the entire campaign, from initial access to lateral movement and launching PHP webshells.
• In some instances, researchers found political messages during the destructive stage, raising questions about a possible false-flag operation.
